A_runtime.reason: Source review only; no browser, build or tests ran in this lane. The earlier d22-recognition-readonly-001 receipt exited nonzero before this change and did not establish a positive fixture or UI acceptance.

positive_evidence: The runner reads the real Saved captures list after real UI organization selection, uses the list's url:canonical_identity alias, and clicks the actual Load more button for later pages. Point recognition still requires an unaliased canonical_identity and matching real Open target.

Discovery reports only fixed categories, counts and query-shape booleans; Source IDs, URLs, hostnames, DNS answers, organization names and response bodies remain in memory. The loop has a configurable page count cap and reports a separate page-budget outcome.

Candidate navigation requires HTTPS, no embedded credentials or nonstandard port, and public DNS answers. The page route rejects non-GET/HEAD page requests and checks redirect destinations. Redirect or exact-identity mismatch remains unverified rather than accepted. No Capture, Save, checkpoint access or database write is added.

findings.title: Absent Load more does not prove the backend list is exhausted
findings.evidence: discoverFixture sets exhausted=true and emits no_eligible_existing_source_in_workspace whenever the UI has zero Load more buttons. SavedCapturesView shows Load more only in its nonempty captures branch, while listSavedCaptures can return a full 40-row page with every row filtered as superseded or unreadable. That state has no button despite a full backend page and possible later Sources. The runner already records rowCount and limit but ignores them for this classification.
findings.required_repair: Set exhausted only when the observed backend page is shorter than its limit. If a full page has no usable Load more control, report a distinct pagination-blocked/unverified result, without claiming no eligible Source exists.

findings.title: A second list response is not proven to be the requested cursor page
findings.evidence: After clicking Load more, discoverFixture accepts the first completed same-organization list GET after since. sourceQuery records cursorPresent but the loop never requires it on page 2 or later, nor validates the captured limit. A concurrent refresh can be counted as a new page and make pages/rows/categories describe repeated first-page data.
findings.required_repair: For pages after the first, require the actual completed query to contain the expected keyset cursor and page limit; classify any unrelated response or unavailable cursor as unverified.

findings.title: The discovery-time budget is narrower than the reported bound
findings.evidence: The 60-second deadline is checked only inside the row loop. Each list-response and UI-settled wait independently allows 30 seconds, and DNS promises may still be in flight after their Promise.race timeout; five pages can substantially exceed SOURCE_DISCOVERY_TIMEOUT_MS while still discovering a fixture.
findings.required_repair: Use remaining deadline for every list/pagination wait and candidate classification; state any separate DNS-operation bound accurately. A budget expiry must remain unverified.

findings.title: Page-scoped routing alone does not establish a no-write browsing guarantee
findings.evidence: installPublicReadGuard registers page.route, then navigates an arbitrary eligible public Source URL. The owned Chromium context does not block site service workers, and this guard has no context-wide or worker-request check. The code therefore proves only that intercepted page requests use GET/HEAD; it cannot justify an unconditional claim that all page-origin requests are read-only.
findings.required_repair: Constrain navigation to a demonstrated read-only page context or add a reviewed worker-aware network boundary. Keep the report's claim scoped to observed/intercepted requests until that is proven.

B_source.limits: The expanded host/DNS filter is a conservative preflight, not a DNS-rebinding guarantee or proof every GET URL is side-effect-free. No actual qualifying row, later page, redirect, or workspace transition was observed in this review. Late Save and real service-failure recovery remain unverified.
